sections.content:
39,155 people

were counted on the census as "other health professionals" in England and Wales in March 2021.
People who do this type of work may perform a variety of other health-related professional occupations not elsewhere classified.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "other health professionals", 15.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "other health professionals" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.title: The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years
sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "other health professionals" included:

  • quality control and planning engineers
  • environment professionals
  • engineering project managers and project engineers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "other health professionals" there were more women than men (76.4% compared with 23.6%).

This means "other health professionals" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health professionals".

Men made up 23.6% and women made up 76.4% of "other health professionals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "other health professionals" included:

  • early education and childcare services proprietors
  • social services managers and directors
  • library clerks and assistants

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "other health professionals" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "other health professionals" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "other health professionals", 11.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (71.5% compared with 28.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (92.5%) than self-employed (7.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
